content: # Hosted runs: every run of a remote session in its own run container, ending in a PR ## What to build When a session's host is remote (`host.kind === "remote"`: a Docker or hosted session), `POST /api/runs/:ws` no longer runs the engine in the session. It checks `GM_MAX_RUN_CONTAINERS`, pushes the session branch (`host.pushBranch`), asks the provisioner for a run container (`ctx.provisioner.acquireRun`), clones the session branch there (`runHost.prepare({ existing: })`), and starts the engine in it. A background monitor (`HostedRuns`) watches the run; when it is `applied` it runs the existing Create PR code inside the run container (branch `gm/`, spec moved to `docs/prd/done/`, PR into the session branch), archives the run (row + folder blob through `ctx.runArchive`), and releases the container (`releaseRun`). A run that ends without applying (failed, aborted) is archived and released too. The session's own files are never touched. The run page, run listing and run detail of a live hosted run are served from the run container; the Start run drawer hides the "Run in sandbox" toggle for remote hosts and warns "Uncommitted changes in acme/api are not part of the run." Local hosts keep today's behaviour exactly (toggle, local Docker sandboxes of KAN-88). Nothing under `packages/graph-execution/src` may change. What dependencies already delivered (read these files first): - Workspace host (`src/server/host/types.ts`): `WorkspaceHost` with `kind: "local" | "remote"`, `prepare({ repo, branch, cloneUrl?, auth? })`, `startEngine({ workspaceId, args, env, timeoutMs })` → `EngineStart`, `stat`, `readFile`, `listFiles`, `listRuns`, `runDetail`, `git`, `changes`, `pushBranch(workspaceId, { auth? })`, `HostError(status, message)` (any `HostError` thrown in a route answers its status with `{ error }`); `AppContext.hostFor(workspaceId, user)`. `pr.ts` is host-based: `prStatus`/`startPr`/`currentJob` take `(ctx, us, host, ws: { id, forge, fullPath }, runId, …)` and `runPrJob` moves the spec with `moveSpecToDoneGit` (`specdone.ts`) through `host.git`. `runs.ts` exports `attachPr`, `attachPrs`, `newestFirst`. - Workspace agent (`src/server/host/remote.ts`): `RemoteWorkspaceHost(url, token)` with `viewTarget(workspaceId, runId) → { url, headers }`; `src/server/agent/server.ts` `startAgent({ port, workspacesDir, token, graphExecutionBin?, loginHome? }) → { url, close }`; `proxy.ts` exports `pipeToUpstream(req, reply, target, pathAndSearch)`. - Sessions core: `src/server/sessions/provisioner.ts` (`SessionProvisioner.acquireRun({ user, sessionId, runId }) → WorkspaceHost`, `releaseRun({ user, runId })`, `LocalProvisioner`), `src/server/sessions/sessions.ts` (`SessionManager`, including the "ending waits while a run of the session is live" check), session records `us.get().sessions[id] = { id, repo: RepoRef, workspaceId, branch, state, startedAt, error? }`, `AppContext.provisioner`, `AppContext.sessions`, `buildApp({ provisioner?, store?, runArchive? })`. - Docker sessions: `src/server/sessions/docker-provisioner.ts` (`DockerProvisioner`; `acquireRun` is idempotent for a running `gm-r-`), `sessions/runtime.ts` (`RuntimeProvisioner`). - Run archive: `src/server/blobs.ts` (`BlobStore`), `src/server/runarchive.ts` (`interface RunArchive { record(user, workspaceId, runId, row); saveFolder(user, workspaceId, runId, tarGz: Readable); list(user, filter?); get(user, workspaceId, runId); openFile(...) }`, `SqlRunArchive`), `AppContext.runArchive`; the Runs page already lists archived runs and opens a read-only detail for them. Read `runarchive.ts` for the exact row type (status, started_at, ended_at, pr_url, state, summary) and how the local flow builds the tar.gz (reuse its helper if it has one that takes a list of `{ path, content }`). - db-store: `const us = await ctx.store.forUser(req.user)`, `resolveRunHome(workspacesDir, us, id)`, `connFor`/`clientFor(ctx, us, kind)`, test helpers `memoryDb()`, `testStore()`, `appWithLogin`. ## Context: files to read before implementing - `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/runs.ts` (start route ~lines 122–228 as refactored: body schemas lines 18–33, `newRunId`, `START_TIMEOUT_MS`, the sandboxed and non-sandboxed branches, `saveDefaults`) — where the hosted branch goes. - `apps/graph-manager/src/server/pr.ts` (`PrJob`, `PrError`, `prStatus`, `preparePr` (branch validity + `refs/heads/` must not exist), `runPrJob` steps checkout/commit/push/create, `startPr`, the `prs[`${ws.id}/${runId}`]` record) and `routes/pr.ts` — Create PR, reused unchanged. - `apps/graph-manager/src/server/specdone.ts` — the spec move into `docs/prd/done/` (already part of `runPrJob`). - `apps/graph-manager/src/server/proxy.ts` (`proxyRoutes`, `pipeToUpstream`) — the run-page proxy to extend for hosted runs. - `apps/graph-manager/src/server/runs.ts` (`RunSummary`, `RunDetail`, `viewUrlOf`, `attachPr`) — what the listing returns. - `apps/graph-manager/src/server/store.ts` (`dataSchema`) — add `hostedRuns` (add, do not rewrite; siblings edit the same schema). - `apps/graph-manager/src/server/config.ts` — add `GM_MAX_RUN_CONTAINERS` (add, do not rewrite). - `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/inspect.ts` (`WorkspaceInspection`, `GET /api/workspaces/:id/inspect`) and `apps/graph-manager/src/web/types.ts` (lines 48–53 `WorkspaceInspection`). - `apps/graph-manager/src/web/pages/StartRunDrawer.tsx` (lines 105–110 state, 175–197 inspect fetch, 343–370 `sandboxEnabled`/`sandboxOn` and the POST body, 441–446 the workspace info hint, 554–600 the sandbox toggle block) and `StartRunDrawer.test.tsx` — the UI change. - `apps/graph-manager/src/server/tar.ts` (`tarArchive(entries, owner)`) and `node:zlib` `gzipSync` — building the folder blob from host reads. - `apps/graph-manager/scripts/fake-forge.mjs` (lines 1–10, 64–140): bare repos cloned over `file://`, `pulls`, 422 when the PR head branch is missing — the forge for tests. - `apps/graph-manager/src/server/sandbox.e2e.test.ts` (lines 1–100) — running the real built engine with `--provider fake` and the `diamond` fixture from `packages/graph-execution/src/__fixtures__/`, polling helpers, skip rule when the engine is not built. ## Patterns to follow **Exact messages:** ```ts // GM_MAX_RUN_CONTAINERS=N and the user already has N active hosted runs: throw new HostError(409, `You have ${limit} sandboxed runs. Wait for one to finish or stop it.`); // UI warning (Start run drawer, remote host, changes > 0), repo = the session's `${owner}/${name}`: `Uncommitted changes in ${repo} are not part of the run.` // push of the session branch failed before the run: throw new HostError(409, `Could not push ${branch} before the run: ${error}`); ``` **Stored record (store.ts dataSchema, keyed by runId):** ```ts hostedRuns: z.record(z.string(), z.object({ runId: z.string(), sessionId: z.string(), workspaceId: z.string(), /** The session branch: the run starts from its last pushed commit and its PR targets it. */ branch: z.string(), state: z.enum(["starting", "running", "finishing", "done", "failed"]), startedAt: z.string(), endedAt: z.string().optional(), prUrl: z.string().optional(), prError: z.string().optional(), prTitle: z.string().optional(), prBody: z.string().optional(), error: z.string().optional(), })).default({}), ``` Active = `starting | running | finishing`; the cap counts active records of the user. **Config:** `GM_MAX_RUN_CONTAINERS` optional integer ≥ 1 → `Config.maxRunContainers?: number`; unset = no cap. Invalid → follow how the file reports other bad integers (e.g. `invalid GM_MAX_RUN_CONTAINERS: …`). **Error handling:** route errors as `HostError`; the monitor never throws — it records `error` on the record, logs with `console.error`, and always calls `releaseRun` in a `finally`. **Test pattern:** a test provisioner that hands out in-process agents, so no Docker is needed: ```ts class AgentProvisioner implements SessionProvisioner { // acquire: startAgent({ port: 0, workspacesDir: /session, token, graphExecutionBin: BIN, loginHome }) → new RemoteWorkspaceHost(url, token) // acquireRun: a NEW agent on /run-; remembers it; releaseRun closes it and records the runId } const { app, cookie } = await appWithLogin({ githubApiUrl: `${forge.url}/github`, maxRunContainers: 1 }, { provisioner: new AgentProvisioner() }); // adapt to appWithLogin's real signature ``` ## Step-by-step tasks ### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/config.ts` and `store.ts` - **IMPLEMENT**: `GM_MAX_RUN_CONTAINERS` and `hostedRuns` as above; add a config test (`3` parses, `0` and `x` are rejected). ### CREATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/hosted-runs.ts` - **IMPLEMENT**: `export class HostedRuns` built in `app.ts` as `ctx.hostedRuns` with `{ ctx, intervalMs = 5000 }`; `start()` sets an unref'd `setInterval(tick)`; `stop()` clears it (add an `onClose` hook). - In memory: `Map`. - `active(us): number` — active records of that user. - `activeFor(user, sessionId): Promise` — an active record for that session. - `start(req-scoped { user, us, session, host, body, args, options })` — the hosted start (below), returns `{ runId, viewUrl }`. - `hostOf(user, workspaceId, runId): WorkspaceHost | undefined` — the run host while active. - `reattach(user)`: for active records of the user missing from memory (control plane restarted), call `ctx.provisioner.acquireRun({ user, sessionId, runId })` (idempotent for a running container) and keep monitoring; if that throws, mark `failed` with the error, archive what can be read (nothing) and `releaseRun`. Call it at the start of `GET /api/runs` and `POST /api/runs/:ws` for that user. - `tick()`: for each in-memory run in state `running`, `detail = await host.runDetail(ws.id, runId)`; `status = detail?.state?.status ?? detail?.summary.status`; when status is `applied`, `done`, `failed` or `aborted` (or `interrupted` with `summary.live === false`), call `finish(run, status)` once (guard with state `finishing`). - `finish`: (1) if `applied`: `const job = await startPr(ctx, us, host, ws, runId, { branch: `gm/${runId}`, title, body, base: session.branch })` where title/body come from `prStatus(...).suggested`; wait until `job.status !== "running"` (poll 200 ms, max 5 min); done → `prUrl = job.pr.url` (startPr already stored `prs[`${ws.id}/${runId}`]`); failed → `prError = job.error`, keep `prTitle`/`prBody` (the branch may already be pushed). Not eligible (e.g. no changes) → `prError = status.reason`. (2) archive: list the run folder through the host — `listFiles` recursively from `.graph-execution/` (walk subfolders with `stat`; skip `worktrees/` and any folder named `.git`; cap 50 MB total) — read each file with `readFile`, build `gzipSync(tarArchive(entries, { uid: 0, gid: 0 }))`, then `ctx.runArchive.record(user, ws.id, runId, row)` with status, times, `pr_url`, the `state` from the detail and the summary, and `ctx.runArchive.saveFolder(user, ws.id, runId, Readable.from(buf))`. (3) `finally`: `ctx.provisioner.releaseRun({ user, runId })`, drop it from memory, record `state: "done"` (applied or done) or `"failed"`, `endedAt`. - **IMPORTS**: `./pr.js`, `./tar.js`, `node:zlib`, `node:stream` (`Readable`), `./host/types.js`, `./identity.js`. ### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/runs.ts` - **IMPLEMENT**: in `POST /api/runs/:ws`, after the home lookup: `const host = await ctx.hostFor(home.id, req.user)`. If `host.kind === "remote"`: - project homes (`project~…`) → `HostError(409, "Runs of project sessions in containers are not supported yet.")` (project sessions arrive in a separate task; keep this explicit); - the session: the record in `us.get().sessions` whose `workspaceId === home.id` and state is not `ending`; none → 404 `unknown workspace`; - `body.sandbox` is ignored (every hosted run is sandboxed); - cap: `ctx.config.maxRunContainers !== undefined && ctx.hostedRuns.active(us) >= limit` → 409 exact message; - validate `tasksDir`/`spec` on the SESSION host with `host.stat` (same 400 messages as the local path); - `pushBranch(home.id, { auth })` with the user's forge token (`connFor(ctx, us, forge)` → `{ forge, token }`); not ok → 409 `Could not push before the run: `; - `runId = newRunId()`; save the record (`starting`); `runHost = await ctx.provisioner.acquireRun({ user: req.user, sessionId, runId })`; `runHost.prepare({ repo: session.repo, branch: { existing: session.branch }, cloneUrl: (await clientFor(ctx, us, forge).getRepo(fullPath)).cloneUrl, auth })`; `runHost.startEngine({ workspaceId: home.id, args, env: { [RUN_ID_ENV]: runId }, timeoutMs: START_TIMEOUT_MS })` with the same `args` as the local path (they include `--web`); a failed start → `releaseRun`, delete the record, answer 400 `{ error, exitCode, output }` as today. Any throw after `acquireRun` → `releaseRun` and delete the record, rethrow. - success → record `running`, `saveDefaults()`, 201 `{ runId, viewUrl: viewUrlOf(home.id, runId) }`. - `GET /api/runs`: append the summaries of the user's active hosted runs (`(await runHost.listRuns(ws)).filter((r) => r.id === runId)`, through `attachPrs`), sorted with `newestFirst`; ended hosted runs come from the archive as the run-archive task already does. - `GET /api/runs/:ws/:runId`: an active hosted run → `runHost.runDetail` (+ `attachPr`). - **GOTCHA**: never call `ctx.sandboxes.start` for a remote host, and never `startEngine` on the session host. ### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/pr.ts` - **IMPLEMENT**: for a hosted run whose container is gone and whose record has `prError` and no `prUrl`: `POST /api/runs/:ws/:runId/pr` retries only the forge call — `clientFor(ctx, us, forge).createPullRequest({ fullPath, head: `gm/${runId}`, base: record.branch, title: record.prTitle, body: record.prBody })`, stores `prs[`${ws}/${runId}`]` like `runPrJob` and `prUrl` on the record, answers 202 `{ job }` with a finished job object (`status: "done"`, steps all `done`) or 409 with the forge error. `GET …/pr` for such a run answers `{ eligible: true, reason: , suggested: { branch: "gm/", title, body, base: record.branch, bases: [record.branch] } }` so the existing PR panel shows the error and a Create PR button. ### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/proxy.ts` - **IMPLEMENT**: before `resolveRunHome`, `const runHost = ctx.hostedRuns.hostOf(req.user, wsId, runId)`; when it is a `RemoteWorkspaceHost`, `const t = runHost.viewTarget(wsId, runId)`, parse `t.url`, and `pipeToUpstream(req, reply, { host: u.hostname, port: Number(u.port || 80), hostHeader: u.host, extraHeaders: t.headers }, `${u.pathname}${rest}${search}`)`. ### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/sessions/sessions.ts` - **IMPLEMENT**: wherever the session decides "a run of the session is live" before releasing (the ending wait), OR it with `await ctx.hostedRuns.activeFor(user, sessionId)`, so closing the last terminal while a hosted run is live ends the session only after the run is finished and released. ### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/inspect.ts` + `src/web/types.ts` - **IMPLEMENT**: `WorkspaceInspection` gains `hosted?: boolean` and `repo?: string`; `GET /api/workspaces/:id/inspect` sets `hosted: true` and `repo: "/"` (from the session record) when `host.kind === "remote"`. ### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/web/pages/StartRunDrawer.tsx` - **IMPLEMENT**: when `info?.hosted`, do not render the `start-run-sandbox` block (toggle, reasons, image), do not send `sandbox` in the POST body, and `commandPreview(..., sandbox)` gets `false`. When `info?.hosted && info.changes > 0`, show `Uncommitted changes in {info.repo} are not part of the run.` under the workspace info hint. Local hosts render exactly as today. - **VALIDATE**: `npm test -w graph-manager -- StartRunDrawer` ### CREATE tests - `apps/graph-manager/src/server/hosted-runs.test.ts` (Linux only and only when the engine is built, like `sandbox.e2e.test.ts`; fake forge; `AgentProvisioner` above; connect GitHub `gh-good`; open a session on `octo/hello` with a new branch through `POST /api/sessions`; in the session commit and push the `diamond` fixture and a spec under `docs/prd/hello.md` through the session host's `git` or a terminal-free helper — `host.git` on the session workspace): 1. Start a run (`POST /api/runs/github~octo~hello` `{ tasksDir: "diamond", spec: "docs/prd/hello.md", provider: "fake" }`) with an uncommitted file in the session: 201; `acquireRun` was called once; the run container's clone is on the session branch at the pushed commit; the session's uncommitted file is still there and the session's files did not change. 2. Poll until the record is `done` (≤ 120 s): the fake forge's `pulls` has one PR with `head: "gm/"` and `base: `; the bare repo's `gm/` contains `docs/prd/done/hello.md` and not `docs/prd/hello.md`; `releaseRun` was called; `GET /api/runs` lists the run (from the archive) and `GET /api/runs//` opens it with `pr.url` set. 3. With `maxRunContainers: 1` and one active run, a second start answers 409 `{"error":"You have 1 sandboxed runs. Wait for one to finish or stop it."}`. 4. A run whose fake script fails a task (`GRAPH_EXECUTION_FAKE_SCRIPT`, see `sandbox.e2e.test.ts` Resume block) ends `failed`: archived, released, no PR. 5. PR failure: make the fake forge refuse (e.g. disconnect GitHub right before finishing, or a base branch the forge rejects) → record `prError`, container released, `POST …/pr` later opens the PR from the pushed `gm/`. 6. While the run is live, `GET /runs///view/state` is proxied from the run container (200 with the run id). - Unit tests without the engine (always run): the cap and the push failure (`pushBranch` stubbed `{ ok: false, error: "rejected" }` → 409 `Could not push before the run: rejected`), project home on a remote host → 409, a local host still starts the engine locally (`acquireRun` never called, toggle path unchanged). - `StartRunDrawer.test.tsx`: with `/api/workspaces/:id/inspect` answering `{ branch, changes: 2, hosted: true, repo: "acme/api" }` the toggle is absent and `Uncommitted changes in acme/api are not part of the run.` is shown; without `hosted` the toggle is present as today. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] With a remote host, every run gets its own run container from `acquireRun`; the toggle is hidden and `sandbox` is ignored; local hosts are unchanged. - [ ] The run starts from the session branch's last pushed commit (`pushBranch` first); the session's files are never changed. - [ ] An applied hosted run ends with a PR from `gm/` into the session branch, the spec moved to `docs/prd/done/`, the run archived with its PR link, and the container released; a failed or aborted run is archived and released without a PR. - [ ] If opening the PR fails, the pushed `gm/` stays, the error shows, Create PR retries it later, and the container is released anyway. - [ ] With `GM_MAX_RUN_CONTAINERS=3` and 3 active hosted runs, `POST /api/runs/:ws` answers 409 `{"error":"You have 3 sandboxed runs. Wait for one to finish or stop it."}`; unset = no cap. - [ ] The Start run drawer shows "Uncommitted changes in acme/api are not part of the run." for a remote host with uncommitted changes. - [ ] Closing a session's last terminal while its hosted run is live ends the session only after the run is released. - [ ] Nothing under `packages/graph-execution/src` changes. - [ ] Tests pass: `npm test -w graph-manager -- hosted-runs StartRunDrawer runs config` ## Validation commands ```bash npm run typecheck && npm run lint npm run build -w graph-execution npm test -w graph-manager -- hosted-runs StartRunDrawer runs pr proxy config sessions git diff --stat -- packages/graph-execution/src # must be empty ``` ## Addendum (coordination with sibling tasks) - Task 11 (project sessions) is now a dependency. Remove the 409 "Runs of project sessions in containers are not supported yet." Instead, a project run on a remote host acquires one run container, prepares it with `prepare({ project, branch: { existing: } })`, runs the suite there, and on `applied` opens one linked PR per changed repository into each repository's session branch, using the existing project Create PR logic (`project-pr.ts`) executed inside the run container (add an agent route for it next to the single-repo Create PR route this task adds). Test it with a two-repo project against bare remotes and the fake forge. - Custom reviewers: before starting the engine in a run container, write the run owner's reviewers file (the same content `writeReviewersFile` in `src/server/reviewers.ts` writes locally, from their `UserStore`) into the container and set the reviewers env variable the local run sets (`REVIEWERS_ENV` in `routes/runs.ts`), so hosted runs use the user's reviewers.
